model.rationale: Min combines a Democratic-leaning district, incumbency, and a lopsided money advantage, and both major prediction markets price his win chances in the mid-90s. With no polling available, the forecast rests on those structural edges and stops short of calling the seat fully safe.
model.watch: New polling or a late wave of outside spending behind Le Roux showing a single-digit race would tighten this outlook considerably.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.

overview:
Democratic incumbent Dave Min defends a Southern California seat with a six-point Democratic lean against Republican Jenny Le Roux. Min has raised about $3.4 million and holds $1.9 million on hand, while Le Roux has raised roughly $376,000 with $129,000 available; outside spending on either side has been negligible. No public general-election polls or expert ratings cover this race.

Prediction markets on Kalshi and Polymarket price Min's chances in the mid-90s. The structural picture of district lean, incumbency, and a dominant financial edge points clearly toward Min, though the absence of polling keeps uncertainty elevated. The forecast expects Min to win by a solid but not overwhelming margin, with a small chance of an upset if late dynamics shift.
